Step 2 (Identify prior probability): $P(\text{fraud}) = 1/1000 = 0.001$.

Step 3 (Identify model accuracy): The model flags 95% of transactions. The 95% is the sensitivity (true positives), not the overall accuracy.

Step 4 (Calculate posterior probability): The posterior probability of fraud given a flag is $P(\text{fraud} | \text{flag}) = \frac{P(\text{flag} | \text{fraud}) \cdot P(\text{fraud})}{P(\text{flag})}$.

Step 5 (Check for base-rate neglect): Base-rate neglect occurs when the model's accuracy is so high that it completely overrides the prior probability.
- Numerator: $0.95 \times 0.001 = 0.00095$.
- Denominator: $P(\text{flag}) = P(\text{flag} | \text{fraud}) \cdot P(\text{fraud}) + P(\text{flag} | \text{not fraud}) \cdot P(\text{not fraud})$.
- $P(\text{flag} | \text{not fraud}) = 1 - 0.95 = 0.05$.
- $P(\text{flag}) = 0.00095 + 0.05 \times 0.999 = 0.00095 + 0.04995 = 0.0509$.
- Posterior: $0.00095 / 0.0509 \approx 0.0187$ (1.87%).
